This page follows U.S. O*NET-SOC 37-1012.00, First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers (the fixed index assigns this asset the corresponding Chinese title; the text follows the official occupational scope). Landscaping supervisory roles vary greatly: municipal and park maintenance, golf and sports turf, property and campus landscaping, commercial landscaping and lawn service companies including contracts and quotes, landscape construction and hardscape coordination, nursery and greenhouse production, and cemeteries, botanical gardens, and other specialized sites. Supervisors may lead one crew or arrange multiple sites and machines. Before comparing roles or development paths, check education and experience requirements; pesticide application, machinery operation and landscaping qualifications and training; physical and health requirements and environments, including heat, cold, sun, dust and noise; seasonal overtime and project schedules; and whether contract review, pricing, budgets, and personnel management are included.

Test your interest with a tabletop exercise: given a wholly fictional landscaping shift assignment covering site type and area, plant and lawn conditions, pruning, fertilizing, irrigation or plant protection tasks, available personnel, machinery, chemicals and consumables, plant, fertilizer and chemical inventories and arrivals, one machine fault, chemical misuse or irrigation damage incident, and required scheduling, assignments, safety and quality reviews and records, write pre-shift assignments and safety briefings, work sequences and quality standards, pesticide and machinery use and protective measures, supply and plant allocation and shortage handling, incident response and reporting routes, and quality inspection, contract and record checks. Mark decisions that must be made by site management or appropriately qualified personnel.

Signals worth considering: willingness to lead crews outdoors and on sites over the long term, organize landscaping and maintenance around seasons and weather, and handle scheduling, safety, quality, contracts, and pricing. Signals requiring caution: unwillingness to work outdoors with weather, dust and machinery over the long term, difficulty accepting seasonal overtime and deadline pressure, or imagining the job as only office planning and quoting.
This card is a career exploration reference and does not constitute a hiring decision, ability score, or safety or compliance conclusion.

First decide whether you are willing to make landscaping site management a long-term career: leading crews in parks, courses, campuses and construction sites; arranging landscaping and care around seasons and weather; organizing schedules and assignments; and taking management responsibility for crew competence, plants, machinery, and chemical safety. Test this through the tabletop exercise and seven-day tasks on this page.

The work of first-line supervisors of landscaping, lawn service, and groundskeeping workers follows a cycle of pre-shift assignments and safety briefings, site landscaping and safety, quality and plant condition oversight, plants, chemicals, machinery and shortages, records, contracts and estimates, scheduling and client communication, and personnel and training management. Before shifts, they check pruning, fertilizing, irrigation or plant protection tasks, available personnel, machinery, chemicals and consumables, and plant, fertilizer and chemical inventories and arrivals, then complete assignments and safety briefings. They schedule crews according to priorities, crew and equipment availability and weather, clarifying work sequences, quality standards and area responsibilities. They establish and enforce procedures and standards for performance and safety, patrol greenspaces, courses and campuses, and inspect plants and soil. During work, they supervise projects for adherence to instructions, deadlines and progress, direct landscaping, lawn care and tree and shrub pruning, inspect completed work against specifications, standards and contracts, and assist workers when needed to meet deadlines. They plant or care for vegetation through mulching, fertilizing, watering, pruning or weeding and direct or perform fertilizer, insecticide, herbicide or fungicide mixing and application. They identify diseases and pests, order treatments, and inventory tools, equipment and materials for sufficient quantities and readiness. They direct or assist power tool and equipment maintenance and repairs, design or oversee sprinkler installations, calculate water pressure, valve and pipe coverage needs, and repair irrigation. They install or maintain landscaped areas, including snow removal, concrete curb construction and sidewalk repairs. They review contracts or assignments to determine service, machinery and staffing needs, estimate costs from labor, materials and machinery, maintain project budgets, negotiate fees, and answer customer questions about methods, materials and price ranges. They develop maintenance or renovation plans and schedules with managers or landscape architects and coordinate interdepartmental work with other supervisors. They investigate complaints, verify issues, determine responses, arrange corrective work, and recommend procedural changes. They maintain personnel and project records, prepare activity and personnel reports, approve leave, and process timesheets. They train staff in transplanting, pruning, concrete finishing, equipment use and lawn care, handle hiring, assessments and discipline, and recommend work condition or equipment changes to improve efficiency. Emphases vary considerably: municipal and park work focuses on public greenspaces and seasonal care; courses and sports grounds on turf quality and event timing; property and campuses on client experience and contract performance; service companies on pricing, budgets and deadlines; landscape construction on hardscape and irrigation coordination; and nurseries and greenhouses on plant production and dispatch plans.

entries.answer: This page follows U.S. O*NET-SOC 37-1012.00, First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers (the fixed index assigns this asset the corresponding Chinese title): directly supervising and coordinating landscaping or groundskeeping workers. Work may include reviewing contracts for service, machinery and staffing needs, answering prospective clients' questions about methods, materials and price ranges, and estimating costs from labor, materials and machinery. Duties include establishing and enforcing procedures and standards; scheduling by priorities, crew and equipment availability and weather; inspecting parks, botanical gardens, cemeteries and courses and checking plants and soil; supervising projects for adherence to instructions and deadlines; directing landscaping, lawn care and tree and shrub pruning; checking completed work against specifications, standards and contracts; planting or caring for vegetation through mulching, fertilizing, watering, pruning and weeding; directing or performing fertilizer, insecticide, herbicide and fungicide mixing and application; training staff in transplanting, pruning, concrete finishing, equipment use and lawn care; preparing service estimates and maintaining project budgets; identifying diseases and pests and ordering treatments; inventorying tools, equipment and materials; maintaining personnel and project records; handling hiring, assessments and discipline; assisting workers when needed; preparing activity and personnel reports; investigating complaints and determining responses; approving leave and processing timesheets; coordinating interdepartmental work; directing or assisting power tool and equipment maintenance and repairs; reviewing contracts and assignments for service, machinery and staffing needs; arranging corrective work and recommending procedural changes; developing care or renovation plans with managers or landscape architects; recommending work condition or equipment changes to improve efficiency; answering client questions about methods, materials and prices; installing or maintaining landscaped areas, including snow removal, concrete curbs and sidewalk repairs; designing or overseeing sprinkler installation and calculating water pressure, valve and pipe coverage needs; negotiating fees; and repairing irrigation systems.
entries.question: What do first-line supervisors of landscaping, lawn service, and groundskeeping workers mainly do?

entries.answer: Responsibilities and outputs differ. This occupation is a first-line management role whose main outputs are crew scheduling and assignments, landscaping and care quality and safety reviews, contract estimates, and records. Landscaping workers directly plant, prune, and care for landscapes. Grounds maintenance workers clean grounds and provide routine facility and lawn care. Vegetation pesticide workers mix and apply pesticides. Pest control workers control pests in buildings and premises. Landscape architects produce landscaping designs. Crop, nursery and greenhouse farmworkers produce plants and crops and are outside this occupation's scope.

entries.answer: The on-site supervisor is responsible for landscaping quality, work safety and the management of personnel, plants and machinery during the shift. Matters involving pesticide selection, mixing and application; hazardous chemical handling; machinery, electrical, elevated and near-electricity work; sprinkler system design and water pressure calculations; and labor, employment, tax and contract compliance must be handled according to procedures by appropriately qualified personnel, competent authorities or professional organizations. Pre-shift briefings and landscaping, inspection and project records must be retained under organizational procedures. Employee, customer, contract and estimate information must be processed only to the minimum extent necessary. When using dispatching, estimating, inventory, inspection and recordkeeping tools, their outputs do not constitute plant or quality conclusions or safety determinations. Matters beyond one's authority should be escalated to the site manager. subject.name: First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers
subject.summary: Directly supervise and coordinate landscaping or groundskeeping workers: establish and enforce procedures and work standards for performance and safety; schedule crews by priorities, crew or equipment availability, and weather; inspect parks, botanical gardens, cemeteries, golf courses, and other sites and assess plants and soil; supervise projects for adherence to instructions, deadlines, and progress; direct landscaping, lawn care, and tree and shrub pruning; inspect completed work against specifications, standards, and contracts; plant or care for vegetation through mulching, fertilizing, watering, pruning, and weeding; direct or perform fertilizer, insecticide, herbicide, or fungicide mixing and application; train workers in transplanting, pruning, concrete finishing, equipment use, and lawn care; estimate service costs from labor, materials, and machinery and maintain project budgets; identify diseases and pests and order treatments; inventory tools, equipment, and materials for adequate supply and readiness; maintain personnel and project records; handle hiring, performance assessment, and discipline; assist workers when needed to meet deadlines; prepare work activity and personnel reports; investigate complaints and determine responses; approve leave and process timesheets; coordinate work across departments or organizations with other supervisors; direct or assist power tool and equipment maintenance and repairs; review contracts or assignments to determine service, machinery, and staffing needs; arrange corrective work and recommend procedural changes; develop maintenance or renovation plans and schedules with managers or landscape architects; recommend work condition or equipment changes to improve crew efficiency; answer customer questions on methods, materials, or price ranges; install or maintain landscaped areas, including snow removal, concrete curb construction, or sidewalk repairs; design or oversee sprinkler installation and calculate water pressure, valve, and pipe coverage needs; negotiate service and groundskeeping costs; and repair irrigation systems.
